captions.linkedin:
Stop buying lottery tickets and calling it investing. 📊

3 academic papers, 1 brutal finding: the stocks that look most exciting in your watchlist quietly drag your portfolio down.

Bali, Cakici and Whitelaw (2011) called it the MAX effect. Ang et al. (2006) called it the IVOL puzzle. Kumar (2009) called them lottery stocks. Same conclusion: retail piles in, future returns sag.

Here's the complete screen. No black box:

🔹 MAX FILTER, exclude the top decile of extreme daily gains.
🔹 IVOL GUARD, remove the top quintile of idiosyncratic volatility.
🔹 PRICE FLOOR, cut names trading below 5 dollars.
🔹 MONTHLY REBALANCE, update lottery scores at month-end.
🔹 LOW TURNOVER, only threshold-crossing names churn.

It's a long-only overlay. Bolt it on top of any equity portfolio you already run. The point isn't to find winners, it's to stop funding losers that look like winners.

Why it works: retail demand for skewness is durable, and short-sale frictions keep the mispricing alive. The behavioral bias isn't going away.
